messages:
alex.sre: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting intermittent 502s and high tail latency for hosted inference in eu-west1a. Spike started ~12:07 UTC, still ongoing. seeing ~15% 5xx rate on the api-gateway for that AZ. ticket: #INC-2026-487.
ops-bot: alert: gateway-5xx-rate(eu-west1a) > 10% for 3m — SLO target breached. traces showing ~75% of errors are upstream gateway timeouts.
carla-support: Customer SLA escalation from Acme.ai — they sent a repro: repeated requests to /v1/generate produce 502 + "upstream read timeout". Their request-id: req_8f3a2c. Attached sample curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -d '{\"model\":\"rw1-large\",\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — gets 502 after ~800ms. They tried from eu region.
ben-oncall: I pulled traces for req_8f3a2c — gateway logs show 504/502 returned by edge-proxy when connection to inference node stalled. Backend pool shows retransmits and a handful of connections reset by peer.
maria-neteng: I'm seeing increased retransmit counts and duplicate ACKs on the eu-west1a egress pair to ProviderX. BGP table shows recent AS path change at 12:05 UTC: ProviderX started sending traffic via a different POP (as-path prepending removed). That lines up with the error window.
network-telemetry-bot: netflow sample (simplified): `src=10.32.3.12:443 -> dst=203.0.113.45:52345 proto=TCP pkts=120 syn=0 dupack=14 retrans=9 rtt_avg=48ms rtt_max=450ms` — multiple flows to same provider show dup acks/retransmits.
alex.sre: Can we confirm this is carrier-side (not our infra NIC/driver)? Any interface counters locally?
maria-neteng: Checked host NIC counters on edge gateway hosts — no rx_errors, no drops on our side. Interface counters clean. The retransmits are observed upstream on ProviderX's path (we see increased out-of-order and dupacks on our egress).
ben-oncall: I started a tcpdump on the edge-proxy facing the provider and forwarded a small pcap to eng-net for triage. Snippet shows repeated DUP-ACKs, then server retransmit, then long stall and connection reset.
carla-support: Customer provided additional repro: they saw a pattern where heavy multi-request batches failed but single short requests succeeded. They asked for ETA and if we can failover them to another region.
alex.sre: Short term mitigation options: 1) route affected customer traffic to eu-west1b (we can use route policy to prefer alternative peering for their tenant id). 2) apply a per-customer circuit breaker to reduce retries. 3) ask ProviderX to revert AS path change / open a ticket. Which do we want first?
maria-neteng: I'm opening ticket with ProviderX now (xref: PX-98765) describing dupacks and as-path change at 12:05. Will request immediate reversion or traffic steering. Also will push a temporary BGP community to prefer alternate peer.
ben-oncall: I'll prepare a deploy to update routing policy for Acme.ai to prefer eu-west1b — can do per-tenant at the gateway LB level. Can we get approval for targeted failover?
carla-support: Acme.ai approves failover to eu-west1b, they said they'd accept short DNS / connection switching window.
alex.sre: Approved. Ben — coordinate with prod-deploy to roll a targeted route preference for tenant=acme.ai; set 5-min canary then 100%. Also add a short-term rate-limit 50rps to reduce tail amplification.
ops-bot: deploy started: route-preference-acme-canary (deploy_id=deploy_8743).
ben-oncall: Canary to 5% complete, metrics look better for those requests — 502s dropped to ~1% for canary traffic. Proceeding to 100% over next 10m.
network-telemetry-bot: provider path update: ProviderX responded to ticket: "we see BGP flap / reroute at 12:05 UTC; investigating". They have not yet reverted.
maria-neteng: Even after failover for Acme.ai, generic traffic for other tenants still shows elevated retransmits to ProviderX. We need broader mitigation. Options: shift more egress to ProviderY, apply BGP communities to avoid the affected POPs, or request ProviderX to perform immediate rollback.
alex.sre: Raise infra risk: if ProviderX path instability continues we'll see higher 5xx across AZ. Plan: short-term (today): shift 60% of cross-AZ egress to ProviderY where we have spare capacity. Mid-term: escalate contract/peering review with ProviderX.
carla-support: Open a customer communication draft for impacted customers — status page blurb + suggested workaround (set region preference to eu-west1b or retry policy adjustments).
ben-oncall: Roll completed — now routing 80% of acme.ai traffic to eu-west1b. 5xx for that tenant down to 0.6%. Global 5xx rate in eu-west1a decreased from 15% -> 9% after partial reroute.
network-telemetry-bot: ongoing telemetry: `eu-west1a gateway retransmits 12:40 UTC -> 8:02` — retransmit rate trending down after shift to ProviderY.
maria-neteng: ProviderX confirmed they had misconfiguration in their internal multipath hashing that caused asymmetric microbursts on the path to our POP. They will revert changes and monitor. They asked for our pcap/flows (sent).
alex.sre: Thanks team. Next steps: 1) keep ProviderX ticket open until two hours of stable metrics. 2) schedule a postmortem if any customer had >30m outage impact. 3) update runbook with detection pattern (dup-acks, retransmits + BGP as-path change correlation). 4) consider adding automatic cross-provider reroute if retransmit rate > X for >Y minutes.
carla-support: I'll send customer closure note to Acme.ai and the impacted customer cohort, include repro summary and mitigation.
ben-oncall: capturing logs/traces + pcap in incident artifact. filing post-incident doc.
alex.sre: Closing loop — marking incident as mitigated at 12:52 UTC (routing shifts + ProviderX rollback in progress). Will convert to postmortem if any billing credits or SLA violations apply.
carla-support: Noted. I'll update the incident channel with customer-facing blurb and ticket numbers. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: incident_status: mitigated (incident_id=INC-2026-487)
